title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 235
paragraphs: He answered: “O king, if you are truly taking counsel with me, it is right that I tell you the best course. What if you were to send three hundred ships of your fleet to attack the Laconian coast? There is an island lying near it called Kythera, of which Chilon, one of our wisest men, used to say that it would be of greater benefit to the Spartans if it sank beneath the sea than if it remained above — for he was always anticipating that something would happen from that quarter of the kind I am now describing to you. It was not that he knew of your expedition beforehand, but that he feared equally every armament of men. So let your forces set out from this island and keep the Lacedaemonians in fear; and while they have a war of their own close to their doors, there will be no fear for you that, when the rest of Greece is being conquered by your land army, they will come to the rescue there. Then, after the rest of Greece has been brought into subjection, the Lacedaemonian power will from that moment stand alone and therefore weak. If, however, you do not do this, here is what you must expect: there is a narrow isthmus leading to the Peloponnese, and there you must look for battles more severe than those which have already taken place, since all the Peloponnesians have sworn to a league against you. But if you follow the course I have described, this isthmus and the cities within it will come over to your side without a battle.”
